title: Anchoring bias: your cost basis is irrelevant to the next decision
summary: The speaker says many wheel traders refuse to sell calls below their cost basis, or close trades because they locked in 50%. Both decisions anchor on the past. If a trade has a 99% chance to earn its last 50%, closing it gives that away. Judge each open trade on its odds from today.

params.label: Excess drift over rate
params.help: Your view of annual return above the risk-free rate. Zero = the market view; EV is then about zero.

steps.caption: Today's price. Decisions start here, not at your old cost basis.
The range of possible prices at expiry, from implied volatility.
The one-standard-deviation range: about two-thirds of outcomes.
The short put is far out of the money; little can still go wrong.
If the chance to keep the last 50% is very high, closing early gives it away.
Judge the trade on its expected value from today, not on what you already earned.

takeaways: Your cost basis does not change the odds of the trade from here.
Do not close a high-probability trade only because you have locked in a gain.
Ask what the remaining trade pays and risks today.
caveats: The 99% figure is the speaker's illustration. Real probabilities depend on price, volatility and time left.
